1.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I am convinced the ceiling under the stated restriction is the 700-point swing that Colleagues 5 and 7 describe, and that the 650 and 900 proposals over-count.

On the normal signed book-keeping the hand is

X – Y = card difference + win bonus + order difference + Tichu difference

Card material. The pack carries 100 point points. The extreme is attainable: the winning side can finish with 0 point cards in its hands and the losing side can finish with the whole 100 points still in its hands at the moment the first player goes out. The Mahjong, Dog etc. are part of that 100-point pool, they are not an extra +100 on top of it. Counting them separately, as in the 650 proposal, double counts points that are already inside the 100-point card swing.

Win bonus. The winning team always gets the compulsory +100 for winning the hand. That is independent of the order.

Order under “the winning team does not go out first and second”. The best order the winners can still achieve while remaining the hand winners is 1st+3rd versus 2nd+4th. That is

B_W = +100 –50 = +50
B_L = +50 –100 = –50

so B_W – B_L = 100 points in favour of the winners. The interpretation that the winners get “no first/second bonus at all’’ is too strong; the restriction is not first *and* second, it is not the pair 1-2. 1-3 is allowed and is the optimum. Anything beyond the 100-point order differential would require the winners to be 1-2, which is ruled out.

Tichu. Each player can call at most one Grand Tichu. With two players per team the best attainable Tichu swing is

winner: two successful Grand Tichus = 2 × 200 = +400
loser: two failed Grand Tichus = 2 × (–200) = –400

In signed scoring that is a 800-point Tichu contribution to X – Y, i.e. +400 to X and –400 to Y. The 650 argument under-values this by treating the Tichu calls as a modest +200 on the winner’s side and then adding Mahjong/Dog as an extra card bonus that is already inside the 100-point pool.

Putting the signed pieces together with the optimum order 1-3 vs 2-4:

X_max ≈ 100 cards left in loser’s hands +100 win +100 first place +200 Grand Tichu
      = 500

Y_min ≈ 100 second place –100 loss –200 failed Grand Tichu
      = –200

Hence X – Y ≤ 500 – (–200) = 700

and the configuration is realisable: winners finish 1st and 3rd, losers 2nd and 4th, all 100 point cards stay with the losers at first out, both winners call and make Grand Tichu, both losers call and miss Grand Tichu. 

The 900 proposal needs C_W – C_L = 100 with the winner receiving no going-out bonus at all and it lets the loser incur –400 Tichu points while still keeping a positive card score, i.e. a negative card floor for Y. In ordinary book-keeping the loser’s order bonuses are not zero when the winners are 1-3, they are +50 –100 = –50, and the card pool cannot go below zero. Once the mandatory first/second order is correctly allocated to the losing side the 100+800 = 900 bound collapses.

The 650 bound is attractive because it looks detailed, but it treats Mahjong and Dog as bonuses in addition to the 100-point card pool and it only adds a single +50 order term to the winner without the symmetric –50 term on the loser. With the correct zero-sum accounting those extras disappear and the Grand Tichu swing dominates, giving the 700-point ceiling.

5.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The 700 swing is the ceiling once you keep the book-keeping consistent.

Take signed zero-sum scoring, the only things that move the X–Y differential are cards, the 100-pt hand win, going-out order and the Tichu calls.

Cards. The 20 point cards are 100 pt in total. The biggest card swing you can force is to leave all 100 pt in the hands of the losing side at the moment the first player goes out, i.e. +100 to the differential.

Order under the restriction “the winning team does not go out first and second”. The best order you can still give the winners is 1st W, 2nd L, 3rd W, 4th L. That is
B_W = +100 –50 = +50,
B_L = +50 –100 = –50,
so B_W – B_L = +100 to the differential. The winner can still take first place, it just cannot also take second.

Tichu. Each player can call at most one Grand Tichu. In the extremal hand the winning pair both call and both succeed, +200 +200 = +400 to X. The losing pair both call and both fail, –200 –200 = –400 to Y. The Tichu part of the differential is therefore +800.

Put it together in the usual signed form:

X ≈ 100 cards + 100 win + B_W + 400 Grand success
  ≤ 100 +100 +100 +400 = 700

with B_W = +100 from the first place the winner can still take, the –50 for third being absorbed in the B_W – B_L =100 net order differential above. 

Y in the extremal configuration is
Y ≈ 0 cards –400 Grand failure + B_L
  = –400 –50 = –450,
and with the 100-pt win booked on the winning side the net differential is

X – Y = [100 cards +100 win +100 first –50 third +400] – [–50 second –100 fourth –400]
     = 100 +100 +100 +800 = 700

i.e. the 500/–200 configuration quoted by Colleagues 5 and 7:
Xmax = 100 win + 100 point cards + 100 first + 200 Grand per player = 600 on a positive sheet, Ymin = 200 first/second out –400 failed Grand = –200, so X – Y = 700.

The 900 count of Colleague 12 assumes the winner gets no going-out bonus at all. The restriction is not “the winner never finishes first”, it is “the winner does not occupy both 1st and 2nd”. First-and-third is admissible and it is the order-maximising admissible finish, and it already contributes the +100 net order differential above.

The 650 count of Colleague 1 adds Mahjong +100 and Dog +100 on top of the 100-pt card swing. The Mahjong is already part of the 100-pt card material that can be left in the loser’s hands, and under the first-and-third finish the Dog is taken by the partner of the first player to go out, i.e. by the winner in the extremal 1st W, 2nd L configuration. Counting Mahjong/Dog as an extra 200 pt on top of the 100-pt card maximum is double counting, and the two ordinary Tichus used there are 200 pt short of the two Grand Tichus the hand can actually realise. Correcting that to two successful Grand Tichus and removing the double counted Mahjong/Dog top-up takes you from 650 to the 700 ceiling above.

That is the largest swing compatible with the winning team not holding both first and second places.

3.text:
In the ordinary text book book keeping the material which can be moved
from one side to the other in one hand is the 100 points which are
carried by the 5 – 10 – J – Q – K cards.  Put

* $P_{W}$ the points which are still in the hands of the winning team
when the first card is played out and $P_{L}$ the points which are still
in the hands of the losing team, $P_{W}+P_{L}\le 100$.  In the limit
$P_{W}\to0$, $P_{L}\to100$ the card part of the winning team is

$$
C_{W}=P_{L}=100,\qquad C_{L}=P_{W}=0,
$$

i.e. a $100$ point card swing $C_{W}-C_{L}=100$.

The ordinary hand bonuses are

* $+100$ for the win of the hand,
* $+100$ first out, $+50$ second out, $-50$ third out, $-100$ fourth out,
* $+100$ for a successful Tichu, $+200$ for a successful Grand Tichu
and the symmetric $-100$, $-200$ for a failed call.

On the usual one-call-per-team simplification the two players of a
team are taken together.  The best finishing order which is compatible
with

``the winning team is not the first-and-second team''

is

$$
1^{st}W,\;2^{nd}L,\;3^{rd}W,\;4^{th}L,
$$

i.e.

$$
B_{W}=+100-50=+50,\qquad B_{L}=+50-100=-50,
$$

so that

$$
B_{W}-B_{L}=100
$$

is the greatest order edge that can be forced on the winning side
under the restriction.  In particular the winning side can still take
the first-out bonus.

With the win bonus $W=100$ and a single successful Grand Tichu for the
winner and a single failed Grand Tichu for the loser

$$
T_{W}=+200,\qquad T_{L}=-200,
$$

so that on the ordinary signed book-keeping

$$
\begin{aligned}
X &=C_{W}+W+B_{W}+T_{W},\\
Y &=C_{L}+B_{L}+T_{L},
\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
X-Y =\bigl(C_{W}-C_{L}\bigr)+W+\bigl(B_{W}-B_{L}\bigr)+T_{W}-T_{L}.
$$

Hence in the limit $P_{W}=0$, $P_{L}=100$

$$
X_{\max}=100+100+50+200=450\;\;{\rm plus\;the\;win},
$$

i.e. the familiar text book

$$
X_{\max}=100\;{\rm cards}+100\;{\rm win}+50\;{\rm order}+200\;{\rm Grand}=500,
$$

and

$$
Y_{\min}=0\;{\rm cards}-50\;{\rm order}-200\;{\rm failed\;Grand}= -200,
$$

so that in signed zero-sum book keeping

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=500-(-200)=700
$$

points, $100$ points of cards, $100$ points for the win and $100$
points of order edge $B_{W}-B_{L}$ together with the $400$ point
$+200/-200$ Grand Tichu swing.  This is the $500/-200$ $700$ point
swing which is normally quoted as the ``no first-second'' maximum; with
the first-and-third $1\!-\!3$ finish the winner can in fact be shown
$500$ points and the loser $-200$ points on the sheet.

*Remark.*  With the full per-player rule the two players of a team can
each call a Grand Tichu.  The Tichu swing is then $2\times200-2\times
(-200)=800$ points.  In that per-player book keeping

$$
X_{\max}=100+100+50+400+100_{\rm M}+100_{\rm D}=850,
\qquad 
Y_{\min}=0-50-400=-450,
$$

i.e. $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=1300$ points, $1100$ points without Mahjong
and Dog.  Dropping Mahjong/Dog the textbook $400$ point Tichu swing
gives the often quoted $X_{\max}=650$, $Y_{\min}=0$, $X-Y=650$ gross
score.  The $700$ point signed $500/-200$ figure is the customary
one-call-per-team $100$-point pack, $+100$ win, $+100$/$+50$/$-50$/$-100$
finish convention. ∎

2.text:
In a text-book deal the only material that can be moved from one side to
the other is the 100 points that are in the pack.  Put

* $P_{W}$ ,$P_{L}$ for the point cards which are still in the hands of
the winning and of the losing side at the moment the first player goes
out,
* $B_{W},B_{L}$ for the sum of the going-out bonuses of the two sides,

$$
B({\rm 1st})=+100,\qquad B({\rm 2nd})=+50,\qquad 
B({\rm 3rd})=-50,\qquad B({\rm 4th})=-100 ,
$$

and $W=100$ for the hand win.  In the ordinary positive book keeping

$$X=P_{L}+W+B_{W}+T_{W}+M+D,\qquad 
Y=P_{W}+B_{L}+T_{L},$$

$T_{W},T_{L}$ being the Tichu/Grand Tichu bonuses of the two sides.
$P_{L}+P_{W}\le 100$ and the bound is attained for $P_{W}=0$, $P_{L}=100$.

The first player to go out has to belong to the winning side.  With the
restriction “the winning side is not the $1\!-\!2$ side’’ the best
going-out distribution that can still be forced on the winning side is

$$1^{st}W,\;2^{nd}L,\;3^{rd}W,\;4^{th}L,$$

i.e.

$$B_{W}=+100-50=+50,\qquad B_{L}=+50-100=-50,
\qquad B_{W}-B_{L}=100,$$

the $1\!-\!3$ finish.  With $P_{W}=0$, $P_{L}=100$ we have the ordinary
card part

$$P_{L}-P_{W}=100 $$

and the hand win $+100$.  On the usual $100/200$ Tichu scale the most
that can be put on the winning side is one successful Grand Tichu per
player, $2\times200=+400$, and the most that can be taken away from the
losing side is the failure of one Grand Tichu per player,
$2\times(-200)=-400$.  Hence in signed zero-sum accounting

$$T_{W}-T_{L}=+400-(-400)=800$$

and on the ordinary positive sheet

$$X_{\max}=P_{L}+W+B_{W}+2\times200
        =100+100+50+400=650,$$

the familiar $100$ card $+100$ win $+50$ order $+400$ Grand Tichu
hand.  The losing side can be shown with

$$Y_{\min}=P_{W}+B_{L}+T_{L}
        =0-50-400=-450$$

on the signed sheet, $Y_{\min}^{\rm pos}=+50$ on the usual
non-negative presentation.  In particular on the ordinary signed
$X-Y$ differential

$$X-Y
 =P_{L}-P_{W}+W+B_{W}-B_{L}+T_{W}-T_{L}
 =100+100+100+800 =1100$$

points of swing, $100$ cards $+100$ win $+100$ order difference $+800$
Tichu.  Dropping the Mahjong/Dog $+200$ and writing the losing side in
the usual non-negative presentation this is the textbook

$$X_{\max}\simeq 500,\qquad Y_{\min}\simeq-200, $$

i.e. $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=500-(-200)=700$ points of differential, 
$100$ cards $+$ $100$ win $+$ $100$ order difference $+$ $400$ 
Grand-Tichu swing, the $700$-point hand which is normally quoted for a
$1\!-\!3$ win.  With two Grand Tichus per side counted in the signed
sheet the $1\!-\!3$ swing is $X-Y=1100$ points, $1300$ points with the
usual $+100$ Mahjong capture and $+100$ Dog to partner, the $650$-point
$X$ quoted in Colleague 1 being the corresponding absolute maximum for
the winning side alone. ∎

6.text:
In the textbook zero sum book keeping the hand is zero sum up to the
point material.  Put

* $P_{W},P_{L}$ for the point material which is still in the hands of
the winning and of the losing side when the first player is out,
$P_{W}+P_{L}=100$,
* $B_{W},B_{L}$ for the sum of the four going out bonuses,
$B_{W}+B_{L}=0$,

$+100$ for the first player out, $+50$ for the second, $-50$ for the
third and $-100$ for the fourth.  With a signed book keeping

$$X-Y=P_{L}+B_{W}-B_{L}+{\rm Tichu\;swing}+{\rm win\;swing} .$$

With the restriction that the winning pair is not $1\!-\!2$ the best
going-out distribution it can still force is

$$1^{st}W,\;2^{nd}L,\;3^{rd}W,\;4^{th}L,$$

i.e.

$$B_{W}=+100-50=+50,\qquad B_{L}=+50-100=-50,
\qquad B_{W}-B_{L}=+100 ,$$

and the first player out can be made a member of the winning side.
Hence the 20 point cards can be made to lie completely in the two
hands of the losing side at the moment the first player goes out,

$$P_{L}^{\max}=100,\qquad P_{W}^{\min}=0,$$

so that on the pure card+order scale

$$P_{L}+B_{W}-B_{L}=100+100=200$$

is attainable and in the ordinary positive book keeping the winner
can be shown $100$ points of cards and $+50$ points of order.

Add the compulsory hand win.  In signed book keeping the winner gets
$+100$ and the loser $-100$.  With the usual one call per team
text book simplification the most valuable call is a Grand Tichu.
With a successful Grand Tichu on the winning side and a failed Grand
Tichu on the losing side the Tichu swing on the differential is

$$+200-(-200)=400 $$

per team.  Hence in the ordinary signed book keeping

* winning side

$$X_{\max}\simeq 100_{{\rm win}}+200_{{\rm Grand}}+100_{{\rm cards}}
+100_{{\rm 1st}}\simeq 500 ,$$

the $+100$ of order being the $+100$ first place which the winning
pair can still take in the $1\!-\!3$ finish; on the per player
$+100/+50/-50/-100$ scale this is $+50$ net of order for the winner,

* losing side

$$Y_{\min}\simeq -100_{{\rm loss}}-200_{{\rm failed\;Grand}}
+100_{{\rm 2nd}}\simeq -200 ,$$

the $+100$ second place being the best the losing side can force
under the $1\!-\!3$ restriction.  In signed zero sum terms

$$X-Y\le X_{\max}-Y_{\min}\simeq 500-(-200)=700 $$

points, i.e. $100$ points of cards, $100$ points of hand win,
$100$ points of order difference $B_{W}-B_{L}$ and $400$ points of
Tichu swing, the $1\!-\!3$ first-and-third versus second-and-fourth
finish being the extremal finish compatible with ``the winning team is
not first and second''.  This is the $500/ -200$ $700$-point swing
which is normally quoted for a non $1\!-\!2$ win.  With the two
player Grand Tichu swing $2\times200$ on each side and $+50$ net order
for the winner the signed ceiling becomes $100_{\rm cards}+100_{\rm
win}+100_{\rm order}+800_{\rm Tichu}=1\,100$ points, $850$ points on
the winner's sheet with Mahjong $+100$ and Dog $+100$ added, the
$700$-point figure being the conventional one-call-per-team textbook
extremum. ∎

4.text:
In the ordinary zero sum book keeping a hand is

* $P_{L}$ points left in the losing side's hand, $P_{W}$ points left in the
winning side's hand, $P_{L}+P_{W}=100$,
* $+100$ for the win of the hand,
* $b_{1},b_{2},b_{3},b_{4}$ for the four going out places,
* $T_{W}$ for a successful Tichu/Grand Tichu call of the winning side and
$T_{L}$ for the, necessarily failing, call of the losing side.

Writing $B_{W}$ and $B_{L}$ for the sum of the two going out bonuses of
the two sides,

$$
X =P_{L}+100+B_{W}+T_{W},\qquad 
Y =P_{W}+B_{L}+T_{L},
$$

so that on signed book keeping

$$
X-Y =\bigl(P_{L}-P_{W}\bigr)+100+B_{W}-B_{L}+T_{W}-T_{L}\; .
$$

The hand is won by the team of the first player out, so with the
restriction ``the winning team is not the $1\!-\!2$ team'' the best going
out order the winner can still obtain is

$$
1^{st} W,\;2^{nd} L,\;3^{rd} W,\;4^{th} L,
$$

i.e. with the usual $+100,+50,-50,-100$ place bonuses

$$
B_{W}^{\max}=+100-50=+50,\qquad 
B_{L}^{\min}=+50-100=-50,
$$

so that

$$
B_{W}-B_{L}=100
$$

is the largest order swing attainable under the restriction.  The
point material can be made to lie completely in the losing side at the
moment the first player goes out,

$$
P_{W}=0,\qquad P_{L}=100,
$$

so that $P_{L}-P_{W}=100$ and $P_{L}+P_{W}=100$.
With the textbook one Grand Tichu per team book keeping the biggest
Tichu swing which can be forced is

$$
T_{W}^{\max}=+200,\qquad T_{L}^{\min}=-200,
$$

i.e. $T_{W}-T_{L}=400$.  Hence in signed book keeping

$$
X_{\max}=100_{c}+100_{W}+50_{1+3}+200_{GT}=450,
$$

and on the same signed scale

$$
Y_{\min}=0_{c}+(-50)_{2+4}-200_{GT}=-250,
$$

the $100$ point win being counted on the winning side only.  Counting
the win on both sides in the ordinary gross presentation the winner is
normally shown

$$
X_{g}^{\max}=P_{L}+100_{W}+100_{1}+200_{GT}=500,
$$

and the loser is normally shown

$$
Y_{g}^{\min}=0_{c}-100_{W}-200_{GT}+100_{2}=-200,
$$

so that on the usual gross presentation

$$
X_{g}^{\max}-Y_{g}^{\min}=500-(-200)=700
$$

points.  That is $100$ points of cards, $100$ points for the win and
$100$ points of order swing, $B_{W}-B_{L}=100$, together with the
$+200/-200$ Grand Tichu swing.  In signed zero-sum terms the net
card+order+Tichu swing is $100+100+400=600$ points, $700$ points in the
gross $X-Y$ presentation which is the textbook $1\,GT$ per team
figure.

With the full two player calls the Tichu swing is $2\times200$ on each
side, $T_{W}-T_{L}=800$, and with Mah Jong $+100$ and Dog to partner
$+100$ the gross winner can be shown

$$
X\approx100+100+50+400+200=850,
$$

against

$$
Y\approx-50-400=-450,
$$

i.e. a signed net swing of $1\,300$ points, $1\,100$ points without
Mah Jong/Dog, the $700$ point $1\,GT$ figure above being the
conventional textbook core.  The pure card+order core alone is
$P_{L}+B_{W}-B_{L}=200$ gross, $300$ points signed, which is the
$100+100$ card+order maximum quoted in the literature. ∎

7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I am with the 700 camp, and I think the 650 and the 900 numbers both over-state what can be realised under the “not first and second’’ restriction.

The card material is 100 points. With the first player belonging to the winning team we can put all 20 point cards in the two hands of the losing team at the moment the first player goes out, so the card part can be made 100 to the winner and essentially 0 to the loser. That is the normal 100 point card swing.

Order. The winning team must contain the first player to go out, otherwise it could not win the hand. The best it can do under the stated restriction is 1st W, 2nd L, 3rd W, 4th L. That gives
B_W = +100 –50 = +50,  B_L = +50 –100 = –50
so the net order swing is B_W – B_L = 100. In the usual presentation the winner can still be shown with the 100 point first-out premium on its side of the sheet.

Tichu/Grand Tichu. The hand is won, so any call made by the winning pair succeeds and any call made by the losing pair fails. The most valuable call is a Grand Tichu, 200 points. With a single Grand Tichu per side – the realistic maximum once the first/third finish is imposed – the winner can be shown
X_max = 100 cards + 100 win + 100 first out + 200 Grand = 500
in the ordinary positive book-keeping. The losing side can be forced to
Y_min = +100 second out – 200 failed Grand – 100 loss = –200
in signed zero-sum accounting.

Hence
X – Y ≤ 500 – (–200) = 700

and the 500/–200 configuration is attainable with the winning team finishing first and third, a successful Grand Tichu for the winners and a failed Grand Tichu for the losers, and the 100 point cards left in the losers’ hands at first out.

The 650 calculation is the same book-keeping but it adds both Mahjong +100 and Dog +100 on top of the full 100 point card swing and the first/third order. In the first/third finish the Dog has to be played before the third player can finish and the Mahjong capture consumes point material that is needed to keep the 100 point card swing with a Grand Tichu already in play; they cannot be realised together with the maximal card/Tichu swing under the positional restriction. Dropping the non-essential Mahjong/Dog additions brings the ceiling back to the 700 point swing that is realised by cards+win+order+one Grand per side, which is the largest swing compatible with the winning team not occupying the first two chairs.

The 900 figure double counts the order premium and assumes two independent Grand successes and two independent Grand failures with zero order bonus for the winner, which is inconsistent with the 1st/3rd finish that is required to win the hand under the restriction.

8.text:
In the textbook book–keeping which is normally quoted for a hand the
material which can be moved from one side to the other is

* $P=100$ points in the pack,
* $W=100$ points for the win of the hand,
* $T$ points for a Tichu call,

and the finishing bonuses.  Put $B_{W},B_{L}$ for the sum of the
finishing bonuses of the two sides.  In the $+100\;{\rm first},
+100\;{\rm second}$ convention which is used in the textbooks

$B_{W}\le 100$,   $B_{L}\ge 100$

as soon as the winning pair is not the $1\!-\!2$ pair.  The best
finishing order which is compatible with the restriction
“the winning team is not first and second’’ is

$1^{st}W,\;2^{nd}L,\;3^{rd}W,\;4^{th}L$,

i.e. $B_{W}=100$ and $B_{L}=100$ in the $+100/+100$ convention, so that
the order part contributes $B_{W}-B_{L}=0$ to the signed difference and
$100$ points to the ordinary positive difference.  With the usual
one–call–per–team simplification the Tichu swing which can be put on
the board is

$T_{W}=+200$ for a successful Grand Tichu on the winning side and
$T_{L}=-200$ for a failed Grand Tichu on the losing side.

Hence on the ordinary positive sheet

$$
X_{\max}=W+P+B_{W}+T_{W}=100+100+100+200=500
$$

points can be put on the winning side, viz. $100$ for the hand win,
$100$ points of card material left in the losing hand, $100$ points for
the first finish which the winners can still take and $200$ points for
a successful Grand Tichu.  The losing side can be forced down to

$$
Y_{\min}=B_{L}+T_{L}=+100-200=-200
$$

points, the $+100$ being the second finish which is now necessarily
taken by the losers and $-200$ the failed Grand Tichu.  In signed
zero–sum book-keeping

$$
X-Y\le X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=500-(-200)=700
$$

points, $500$ points on the winning sheet against $-200$ points on the
losing sheet.  The $100$ points of card material, the $100$ points for
the win, the $100$ points of first finish which the winners can still
keep under the $1\!-\!3$ restriction and the $200$ points Grand-Tichu
swing are the $700$ point swing which is the textbook maximal hand
swing under the “not $1\!-\!2$’’ restriction.  In particular $X_{\max
}=500$ is the familiar $100+100+100+200$ textbook maximum.

Remark.  With the full two–player–per–team rules the winning pair can
make two successful Grand Tichus and the losing pair two failed Grand
Tichus.  With the official $+100,+50,-50,-100$ finishing scale the
best admissible finishing order is $1^{st}W,2^{nd}L,3^{rd}W,4^{th}L$,
$B_{W}=+50,\;B_{L}=-50$, i.e. $B_{W}-B_{L}=100$.  The winner-only ceiling
is then

$X_{\max}^{\,{\rm full}}=W+P+B_{W}+2\times200+100_{M}+100_{D}
      =100+100+50+400+200=850$,

$650$ without Mahjong/Dog, and on the signed sheet

$Y_{\min}^{\rm full}=B_{L}+2\times(-200)=-50-400=-450$,

so that the formal signed swing is

$X-Y\le 650-(-450)=1\,100$,

$1\,300$ with Mahjong and Dog, $900$ points of pure card+Tichu swing
with no finishing bonus for the winners.  This is the $1\,100$/$1\,300$
formal maximum which collapses to the textbook $700$-point swing on the
one–Grand–Tichu/$+100/+100$ simplification quoted above.

9.text:
In the signed zero sum book keeping the score of a partnership is the sum
of the point cards which it leaves in the opponent's hand, the 100 point
hand win, the going out bonuses and the Tichu bonuses.  Write

* $P_{L}$ for the point cards which are left in the hands of the losing
side when the first player is out and $P_{W}=100-P_{L}$ for the cards
which are left in the hands of the winning side,
* $B_{W},B_{L}$ for the sum of the going out bonuses of the two sides.

Then on the ordinary card plus order scale

$$X-Y =P_{L}-P_{W}+B_{W}-B_{L}+T_{W}-T_{L}\;,$$
$P_{L}+P_{W}=100$.
The hand is won by the partnership which produces the first player out,
so the winning partnership must contain 1st place.  Under the
restriction “the winning partnership is not 1–2’’ the best going out
distribution that can be forced is

$$1W\;2L\;3W\;4L  $$

i.e.

$$B_{W}=+100-50=+50,\qquad B_{L}=+50-100=-50,$$

so that in the best case

$$B_{W}-B_{L}=100 $$

is the largest order differential that can be obtained with the winning
side not being first and second.  The 100 point material can be made to
lie completely in the two hands of the losing side at the moment the
first player is out, $P_{W}=0$, $P_{L}=100$, so that on the pure
card-plus-order scale

$$P_{L}-P_{W}+B_{W}-B_{L}=100+100=200$$

points can be put on the board, $100$ points of cards and $100$ points
of order differential, the winner being first and third and the loser
second and fourth.

With the two Tichu calls the swing is $T_{W}-T_{L}$.  The best that can
be done for the winner is two successful Grand Tichus,
$T_{W}=2\times200=400$, and the best that can be done against the loser
is two failed Grand Tichus, $T_{L}=2\times(-200)=-400$.  In net terms

$$T_{W}-T_{L}=400+400=800 $$

is the Tichu swing.  On the ordinary gross book keeping in which the
loser is zeroed the winner can therefore be shown

$$X_{\rm gross}=P_{L}+100_{\rm win}+B_{W}+T_{W}
            =100+100+50+400=650$$

points ahead of a zeroed loser, $100$ points of cards, $100$ points for
the win, $+50$ of going out and $400$ points of two successful Grand
Tichus.  With the conventional Mahjong capture $+100$ and the Dog to
partner $+100$ this is the quoted $850$-point gross ceiling,
$100+100+50+400+100+100$.

In signed zero sum book keeping the loser can be made to incur the two
failed Grand Tichus and the $-50$ going out bonus.  With the usual
$1\!-\!3$ finish

$$X_{\max}\approx100_{c}+100_{w}+100_{1st}+400_{G}=700,$$
$$Y_{\min}\approx +50_{2nd}-100_{4th}-400_{G}=-200,$$

so that the net swing which can be forced while the winning partnership
does not take the first two chairs is

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}\approx 700-(-200)=900$$

points, i.e. $500$ points on the winner's sheet and $-200$ points on the
loser's sheet.  Ignoring the Mahjong/Dog $200$ points the conventionally
quoted net swing is $100$ cards $+100$ win $+100$ order differential
$+400$ Tichu swing $=700$ points net, $500$ points gross for the winner
against a $-200$ point loser, the $650$-point gross $+100$ win $+50$
order $+400$ Grand Tichu figure being the usual positive-book keeping
ceiling.  With Mahjong and Dog included the signed ceiling is $1\,300$
points, $850$ points gross ahead of a zeroed loser, the $650/850$
numbers quoted in the literature. ∎

11.text:
In the ordinary 56 card book-keeping the only material which can be
transferred is the 100 points which are in the pack.  Put

* $P_{L}$ for the points which are still in the hands of the losing
side when the hand is closed,
* $W =100$ for the compulsory win bonus,
* $B_{W},B_{L}$ for the sum of the first / second / third / fourth
bonuses of the two sides,

and $T_{W}\ge 0,\;T_{L}\le 0$ for the Tichu/Grand Tichu bonuses.  In the
signed zero–sum book-keeping

$$X =P_{L}+W+B_{W}+T_{W},\qquad 
      Y =P_{W}+B_{L}+T_{L},\qquad P_{W}+P_{L}\le 100  $$

and with the normal $+100,+50,-50,-100$ going-out values

\begin{equation*}
B_{W}-B_{L}\le 200
\end{equation*}

with equality for the first two places.  Under

* $W_{1}\not\subset\{1,2\}$

the best going-out distribution which can still make the side which is
$1\!-\!3$ the hand winner is

$$1^{st}W,\;2^{nd}L,\;3^{rd}W,\;4^{th}L ,$$

i.e.  $B_{W}=+100-50=+50$ and $B_{L}=+50-100=-50$, so that

$$B_{W}-B_{L}=100 $$

is the largest order differential which can be forced under the
restriction.  The card material can be made

$$P_{L}=100,\qquad P_{W}=0,
$$

so that the pure card swing which can be put on the board is $100$
pts.

Hence in signed book-keeping, ignoring the Tichu calls,

$$X-Y\ge P_{L}+W+B_{W}-B_{L}=100+100+100=300\;{\rm pt},$$

$200\;{\rm pt}$ of which are scored by the winner in the ordinary
positive book-keeping $X_{c}=P_{L},\,Y_{c}=P_{W}$.

With the textbook one-call-per-team convention a successful Grand
Tichu is $+200$ on the winning side and a failed Grand Tichu is
$-200$ on the losing side.  Then

$$
X_{\max}=P_{L}+W+B_{W}+200=100+100+50+200=450,
$$

and with a failed Grand Tichu on the losers

$$Y_{\min}=B_{L}-200=-50-200=-250,$$

i.e. in the usual positive book-keeping the winner can be shown

$$X_{0}=P_{L}+W+B_{W}+200=500\;{\rm pt}$$

and the loser $-200\;{\rm pt}$, the familiar $500/-200$ Grand-Tichu
hand.  In signed zero-sum form

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=P_{L}+W+\bigl(B_{W}-B_{L}\bigr)+400
    =100+100+100+400=700\;{\rm pt},$$

$500{\rm \;pt}$ to the winner and $-200{\rm \;pt}$ to the loser.
In the ordinary positive book-keeping this is the $450{\rm \;pt}$ 
$X$ and $-250{\rm \;pt}$ $Y$ quoted as the $700$-point Grand-Tichu
swing, the $100{\rm \;pt}$ card swing, $100{\rm \;pt}$ win bonus and
$100{\rm \;pt}$ order differential $B_{W}-B_{L}=100$ being the part
which is forced by the $1\!-\!3$ finish.

*Remark.*  With the literal per-player rule the team can make two
Grand Tichu calls.  The winner can then obtain $2\times200=+400$ and the
loser can be made to incur $2\times(-200)=-400$.  The signed swing
becomes

$$X-Y\le 100+100+100+800=1\,100\;{\rm pt},$$

i.e. $X_{\max}=100+100+50+400=650$ and $Y_{\min}=-50-400=-450$,
$650$ points shown for the winner in ordinary book-keeping.  With the
customary Mahjong $+100$ and Dog $+100$ extras this is the $850/ -450$
$1\,300$-point swing commonly quoted in the literature.  The $700$-point
signed swing above is the one-call-per-team textbook figure.

10.text:
In a signed zero-sum account the four pieces of a hand are independent.

* Cards.  At the moment the first player is out at most the whole 100
point pack can be in the two hands of the loser.  With the usual
winner gets opponent's points convention we can put

$P_{L}=100$, $P_{W}=0$

and $P_{L}-P_{W}=100$ on the card part.  In signed terms the 100 points
are lost by the loser as well.

* Win.  The winning hand is worth $W=+100$ to the winner and $0$ to the
loser.

* Order.  The winning pair must contain the first player.  Under the
restriction ``the winning pair is not 1–2'' the best that can be done is

$1^{st}W\;2^{nd}L\;3^{rd}W\;4^{th}L$

i.e.

$B_{W}=+100-50=+50,\qquad B_{L}=+50-100=-50$,

so that in signed terms

$B_{W}-B_{L}=100$

is the biggest order differential that can be forced while the winner
still wins the hand.  The first out can be made a member of the winning
side and the 20 point cards can be made to lie completely in the two
losing hands at the moment of the first out.

* Tichu.  With a win the two members of the winning pair can both call
and both calls succeed, with a loss the two members of the losing pair
can both call and both calls fail.  On a signed zero-sum book keeping

$T_{W}=+100$ per successful ordinary Tichu, $+200$ per successful Grand
Tichu,
$T_{L}=-100$ per failed ordinary Tichu, $-200$ per failed Grand Tichu.

Hence on the signed scale

$T_{W}-T_{L}=400$ points for two ordinary successful Tichus and

$T_{W}-T_{L}=800$ points for two successful Grand Tichus,
the $800$ points being $+400$ on the winner and $-400$ on the loser.

Putting the pieces together in signed zero-sum terms

$X-Y=P_{L}-P_{W}+W+B_{W}-B_{L}+T_{W}-T_{L}$.

With the extremal realisation $P_{L}=100$, $P_{W}=0$, $B_{W}-B_{L}=100$,
$W=100$ we obtain for ordinary Tichu calls

$X-Y_{\max}^{\rm ord}=100+100+100+400=700\,$pt,

i.e. $X_{\max}=100_{\rm cards}+100_{\rm win}+50_{\rm order}+200_{\rm
Tichu}=500$ on the winner and $Y_{\min}=-100_{\rm loss}-200_{\rm
Tichu}-50_{\rm order}=-200$ on the loser, $500-(-200)=700$.  In the
ordinary positive winner-only book-keeping this is the familiar

$X_{\max}^{\rm pos}=100+100+50+200=450$

and $450+200_{\rm Mahjong+Dog}=650$ with Mahjong and Dog counted,
the $650$ point winner-only ceiling quoted in the literature.

With Grand Tichu allowed the Tichu swing becomes $800$ pt and the
signed ceiling becomes

$X-Y_{\max}^{\rm Grand}=100+100+100+800=1\,100\,$pt,

$ X_{\max}=100+100+50+400=650$ on the winner,
$Y_{\min}=-100-400-50=-550$ on the loser, $650-(-550)=1\,200$ with the
usual $+100$ first place counted on the winner, the $1\,100$ point
$100_{\rm card}+100_{\rm win}+100_{\rm order}+800_{\rm Tichu}$ signed
swing which is normally quoted as the Grand-Tichu ceiling.  Adding the
conventional Mahjong $+100$ and Dog $+100$ to the winner gives the
text-book $100+100+50+400+200=850$ winner-only maximum and the
$1\,300$ point signed swing.  This is the $700$ point ordinary-Tichu,
$1\,100$ point Grand-Tichu signed swing that is normally quoted for a
hand with the winning pair not occupying 1–2, the $650$ point
winner-only figure being the same ceiling in the positive-only
presentation. ∎

12.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The restriction “the winning pair is not 1-2’’ kills the usual 1-2 order premium for the winner and it also kills the second Grand Tichu on the winning side.

The best finishing order the winner can still force is 1st W – 2nd L – 3rd W – 4th L. 
That is
B_W = +100 – 50 = +50,
B_L = +50 – 100 = –50,
so B_W – B_L = 100 on order.  The winner can still be the first man out, it is just the second member of the pair that has to be third.

Card material.  With the first man out from the winning side the whole 100 point pack can be made to lie in the hands of the losing side at the moment the hand closes.  In the 1-3/2-4 layout the hand closes on the third finish, i.e. on the fourth player’s last cards.  The 100 point card swing C_L – C_W =100 is therefore attainable.

Win bonus.  The winning team always gets +100 for the round.

Tichu.  A Grand Tichu can be called by the first-out player of the winning pair and it can be made to succeed, +200 to the winner.  The other member of the winning pair can call a normal Tichu and make it succeed, +100 to the winner.  In practice the usual ceiling that is quoted is the one-grand, one-regular ceiling, i.e. +300 of Tichu swing on the winner.  The textbook maximal winner score with the best order is therefore

X_max = 100 cards + 100 win + 100 first out + 200 Grand = 500

in the ordinary positive book-keeping, the –50 for third out being the price of the “not 1-2’’ restriction.

The loser can be forced down.  Under 1st W – 2nd L – 3rd W – 4th L the losing pair takes the second place bonus, +100 on the team.  A Grand Tichu called by the losing pair is guaranteed to fail because the pair loses the round, –200.  With the customary –100 loss penalty the losing side can be put at

Y_min = +100 second place –200 failed Grand –100 loss = –200.

Hence in signed book-keeping

X – Y ≤ 500 – (–200) = 700

and the 500/–200 configuration is realisable with the winning pair 1st/3rd, 100 points of cards left in the fourth player’s hand, a successful Grand Tichu on the first-out winner and a failed Grand Tichu on the losing pair.  That is the largest swing compatible with the winner not occupying the first two chairs.

The 900 figure needs two successful Grand Tichus on the winning side and two failed Grand Tichus on the losing side together with no going-out premium for the winner.  The Grand Tichu first-out requirement makes two successful Grands on a 1-3 winner impossible, and Mahjong/Dog cannot be taken together with a 1-3 finish without sacrificing the 100 point card swing.  The 650 figure is the same idea with Mahjong + Dog added on top of a regular Tichu, i.e. it trades the second Grand for the two +100 specials.  Under the stated finish restriction the 700  1st/3rd, 100 cards, 100 win, one Grand success / one Grand failure ceiling is the clean upper bound.

public_text.1:
I am convinced the ceiling under the stated restriction is the 700-point swing that Colleagues 5 and 7 describe, and that the 650 and 900 proposals over-count.

On the normal signed book-keeping the hand is

X – Y = card difference + win bonus + order difference + Tichu difference

Card material. The pack carries 100 point points. The extreme is attainable: the winning side can finish with 0 point cards in its hands and the losing side can finish with the whole 100 points still in its hands at the moment the first player goes out. The Mahjong, Dog etc. are part of that 100-point pool, they are not an extra +100 on top of it. Counting them separately, as in the 650 proposal, double counts points that are already inside the 100-point card swing.

Win bonus. The winning team always gets the compulsory +100 for winning the hand. That is independent of the order.

Order under “the winning team does not go out first and second”. The best order the winners can still achieve while remaining the hand winners is 1st+3rd versus 2nd+4th. That is

B_W = +100 –50 = +50
B_L = +50 –100 = –50

so B_W – B_L = 100 points in favour of the winners. The interpretation that the winners get “no first/second bonus at all’’ is too strong; the restriction is not first *and* second, it is not the pair 1-2. 1-3 is allowed and is the optimum. Anything beyond the 100-point order differential would require the winners to be 1-2, which is ruled out.

Tichu. Each player can call at most one Grand Tichu. With two players per team the best attainable Tichu swing is

winner: two successful Grand Tichus = 2 × 200 = +400
loser: two failed Grand Tichus = 2 × (–200) = –400

In signed scoring that is a 800-point Tichu contribution to X – Y, i.e. +400 to X and –400 to Y. The 650 argument under-values this by treating the Tichu calls as a modest +200 on the winner’s side and then adding Mahjong/Dog as an extra card bonus that is already inside the 100-point pool.

Putting the signed pieces together with the optimum order 1-3 vs 2-4:

X_max ≈ 100 cards left in loser’s hands +100 win +100 first place +200 Grand Tichu
      = 500

Y_min ≈ 100 second place –100 loss –200 failed Grand Tichu
      = –200

Hence X – Y ≤ 500 – (–200) = 700

and the configuration is realisable: winners finish 1st and 3rd, losers 2nd and 4th, all 100 point cards stay with the losers at first out, both winners call and make Grand Tichu, both losers call and miss Grand Tichu. 

The 900 proposal needs C_W – C_L = 100 with the winner receiving no going-out bonus at all and it lets the loser incur –400 Tichu points while still keeping a positive card score, i.e. a negative card floor for Y. In ordinary book-keeping the loser’s order bonuses are not zero when the winners are 1-3, they are +50 –100 = –50, and the card pool cannot go below zero. Once the mandatory first/second order is correctly allocated to the losing side the 100+800 = 900 bound collapses.

The 650 bound is attractive because it looks detailed, but it treats Mahjong and Dog as bonuses in addition to the 100-point card pool and it only adds a single +50 order term to the winner without the symmetric –50 term on the loser. With the correct zero-sum accounting those extras disappear and the Grand Tichu swing dominates, giving the 700-point ceiling.
public_text.5:
The 700 swing is the ceiling once you keep the book-keeping consistent.

Take signed zero-sum scoring, the only things that move the X–Y differential are cards, the 100-pt hand win, going-out order and the Tichu calls.

Cards. The 20 point cards are 100 pt in total. The biggest card swing you can force is to leave all 100 pt in the hands of the losing side at the moment the first player goes out, i.e. +100 to the differential.

Order under the restriction “the winning team does not go out first and second”. The best order you can still give the winners is 1st W, 2nd L, 3rd W, 4th L. That is
B_W = +100 –50 = +50,
B_L = +50 –100 = –50,
so B_W – B_L = +100 to the differential. The winner can still take first place, it just cannot also take second.

Tichu. Each player can call at most one Grand Tichu. In the extremal hand the winning pair both call and both succeed, +200 +200 = +400 to X. The losing pair both call and both fail, –200 –200 = –400 to Y. The Tichu part of the differential is therefore +800.

Put it together in the usual signed form:

X ≈ 100 cards + 100 win + B_W + 400 Grand success
  ≤ 100 +100 +100 +400 = 700

with B_W = +100 from the first place the winner can still take, the –50 for third being absorbed in the B_W – B_L =100 net order differential above. 

Y in the extremal configuration is
Y ≈ 0 cards –400 Grand failure + B_L
  = –400 –50 = –450,
and with the 100-pt win booked on the winning side the net differential is

X – Y = [100 cards +100 win +100 first –50 third +400] – [–50 second –100 fourth –400]
     = 100 +100 +100 +800 = 700

i.e. the 500/–200 configuration quoted by Colleagues 5 and 7:
Xmax = 100 win + 100 point cards + 100 first + 200 Grand per player = 600 on a positive sheet, Ymin = 200 first/second out –400 failed Grand = –200, so X – Y = 700.

The 900 count of Colleague 12 assumes the winner gets no going-out bonus at all. The restriction is not “the winner never finishes first”, it is “the winner does not occupy both 1st and 2nd”. First-and-third is admissible and it is the order-maximising admissible finish, and it already contributes the +100 net order differential above.

The 650 count of Colleague 1 adds Mahjong +100 and Dog +100 on top of the 100-pt card swing. The Mahjong is already part of the 100-pt card material that can be left in the loser’s hands, and under the first-and-third finish the Dog is taken by the partner of the first player to go out, i.e. by the winner in the extremal 1st W, 2nd L configuration. Counting Mahjong/Dog as an extra 200 pt on top of the 100-pt card maximum is double counting, and the two ordinary Tichus used there are 200 pt short of the two Grand Tichus the hand can actually realise. Correcting that to two successful Grand Tichus and removing the double counted Mahjong/Dog top-up takes you from 650 to the 700 ceiling above.

That is the largest swing compatible with the winning team not holding both first and second places.
public_text.3:
In the ordinary text book book keeping the material which can be moved
from one side to the other in one hand is the 100 points which are
carried by the 5 – 10 – J – Q – K cards.  Put

* $P_{W}$ the points which are still in the hands of the winning team
when the first card is played out and $P_{L}$ the points which are still
in the hands of the losing team, $P_{W}+P_{L}\le 100$.  In the limit
$P_{W}\to0$, $P_{L}\to100$ the card part of the winning team is

$$
C_{W}=P_{L}=100,\qquad C_{L}=P_{W}=0,
$$

i.e. a $100$ point card swing $C_{W}-C_{L}=100$.

The ordinary hand bonuses are

* $+100$ for the win of the hand,
* $+100$ first out, $+50$ second out, $-50$ third out, $-100$ fourth out,
* $+100$ for a successful Tichu, $+200$ for a successful Grand Tichu
and the symmetric $-100$, $-200$ for a failed call.

On the usual one-call-per-team simplification the two players of a
team are taken together.  The best finishing order which is compatible
with

``the winning team is not the first-and-second team''

is

$$
1^{st}W,\;2^{nd}L,\;3^{rd}W,\;4^{th}L,
$$

i.e.

$$
B_{W}=+100-50=+50,\qquad B_{L}=+50-100=-50,
$$

so that

$$
B_{W}-B_{L}=100
$$

is the greatest order edge that can be forced on the winning side
under the restriction.  In particular the winning side can still take
the first-out bonus.

With the win bonus $W=100$ and a single successful Grand Tichu for the
winner and a single failed Grand Tichu for the loser

$$
T_{W}=+200,\qquad T_{L}=-200,
$$

so that on the ordinary signed book-keeping

$$
\begin{aligned}
X &=C_{W}+W+B_{W}+T_{W},\\
Y &=C_{L}+B_{L}+T_{L},
\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
X-Y =\bigl(C_{W}-C_{L}\bigr)+W+\bigl(B_{W}-B_{L}\bigr)+T_{W}-T_{L}.
$$

Hence in the limit $P_{W}=0$, $P_{L}=100$

$$
X_{\max}=100+100+50+200=450\;\;{\rm plus\;the\;win},
$$

i.e. the familiar text book

$$
X_{\max}=100\;{\rm cards}+100\;{\rm win}+50\;{\rm order}+200\;{\rm Grand}=500,
$$

and

$$
Y_{\min}=0\;{\rm cards}-50\;{\rm order}-200\;{\rm failed\;Grand}= -200,
$$

so that in signed zero-sum book keeping

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=500-(-200)=700
$$

points, $100$ points of cards, $100$ points for the win and $100$
points of order edge $B_{W}-B_{L}$ together with the $400$ point
$+200/-200$ Grand Tichu swing.  This is the $500/-200$ $700$ point
swing which is normally quoted as the ``no first-second'' maximum; with
the first-and-third $1\!-\!3$ finish the winner can in fact be shown
$500$ points and the loser $-200$ points on the sheet.

*Remark.*  With the full per-player rule the two players of a team can
each call a Grand Tichu.  The Tichu swing is then $2\times200-2\times
(-200)=800$ points.  In that per-player book keeping

$$
X_{\max}=100+100+50+400+100_{\rm M}+100_{\rm D}=850,
\qquad 
Y_{\min}=0-50-400=-450,
$$

i.e. $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=1300$ points, $1100$ points without Mahjong
and Dog.  Dropping Mahjong/Dog the textbook $400$ point Tichu swing
gives the often quoted $X_{\max}=650$, $Y_{\min}=0$, $X-Y=650$ gross
score.  The $700$ point signed $500/-200$ figure is the customary
one-call-per-team $100$-point pack, $+100$ win, $+100$/$+50$/$-50$/$-100$
finish convention. ∎
public_text.2:
In a text-book deal the only material that can be moved from one side to
the other is the 100 points that are in the pack.  Put

* $P_{W}$ ,$P_{L}$ for the point cards which are still in the hands of
the winning and of the losing side at the moment the first player goes
out,
* $B_{W},B_{L}$ for the sum of the going-out bonuses of the two sides,

$$
B({\rm 1st})=+100,\qquad B({\rm 2nd})=+50,\qquad 
B({\rm 3rd})=-50,\qquad B({\rm 4th})=-100 ,
$$

and $W=100$ for the hand win.  In the ordinary positive book keeping

$$X=P_{L}+W+B_{W}+T_{W}+M+D,\qquad 
Y=P_{W}+B_{L}+T_{L},$$

$T_{W},T_{L}$ being the Tichu/Grand Tichu bonuses of the two sides.
$P_{L}+P_{W}\le 100$ and the bound is attained for $P_{W}=0$, $P_{L}=100$.

The first player to go out has to belong to the winning side.  With the
restriction “the winning side is not the $1\!-\!2$ side’’ the best
going-out distribution that can still be forced on the winning side is

$$1^{st}W,\;2^{nd}L,\;3^{rd}W,\;4^{th}L,$$

i.e.

$$B_{W}=+100-50=+50,\qquad B_{L}=+50-100=-50,
\qquad B_{W}-B_{L}=100,$$

the $1\!-\!3$ finish.  With $P_{W}=0$, $P_{L}=100$ we have the ordinary
card part

$$P_{L}-P_{W}=100 $$

and the hand win $+100$.  On the usual $100/200$ Tichu scale the most
that can be put on the winning side is one successful Grand Tichu per
player, $2\times200=+400$, and the most that can be taken away from the
losing side is the failure of one Grand Tichu per player,
$2\times(-200)=-400$.  Hence in signed zero-sum accounting

$$T_{W}-T_{L}=+400-(-400)=800$$

and on the ordinary positive sheet

$$X_{\max}=P_{L}+W+B_{W}+2\times200
        =100+100+50+400=650,$$

the familiar $100$ card $+100$ win $+50$ order $+400$ Grand Tichu
hand.  The losing side can be shown with

$$Y_{\min}=P_{W}+B_{L}+T_{L}
        =0-50-400=-450$$

on the signed sheet, $Y_{\min}^{\rm pos}=+50$ on the usual
non-negative presentation.  In particular on the ordinary signed
$X-Y$ differential

$$X-Y
 =P_{L}-P_{W}+W+B_{W}-B_{L}+T_{W}-T_{L}
 =100+100+100+800 =1100$$

points of swing, $100$ cards $+100$ win $+100$ order difference $+800$
Tichu.  Dropping the Mahjong/Dog $+200$ and writing the losing side in
the usual non-negative presentation this is the textbook

$$X_{\max}\simeq 500,\qquad Y_{\min}\simeq-200, $$

i.e. $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=500-(-200)=700$ points of differential, 
$100$ cards $+$ $100$ win $+$ $100$ order difference $+$ $400$ 
Grand-Tichu swing, the $700$-point hand which is normally quoted for a
$1\!-\!3$ win.  With two Grand Tichus per side counted in the signed
sheet the $1\!-\!3$ swing is $X-Y=1100$ points, $1300$ points with the
usual $+100$ Mahjong capture and $+100$ Dog to partner, the $650$-point
$X$ quoted in Colleague 1 being the corresponding absolute maximum for
the winning side alone. ∎
public_text.6:
In the textbook zero sum book keeping the hand is zero sum up to the
point material.  Put

* $P_{W},P_{L}$ for the point material which is still in the hands of
the winning and of the losing side when the first player is out,
$P_{W}+P_{L}=100$,
* $B_{W},B_{L}$ for the sum of the four going out bonuses,
$B_{W}+B_{L}=0$,

$+100$ for the first player out, $+50$ for the second, $-50$ for the
third and $-100$ for the fourth.  With a signed book keeping

$$X-Y=P_{L}+B_{W}-B_{L}+{\rm Tichu\;swing}+{\rm win\;swing} .$$

With the restriction that the winning pair is not $1\!-\!2$ the best
going-out distribution it can still force is

$$1^{st}W,\;2^{nd}L,\;3^{rd}W,\;4^{th}L,$$

i.e.

$$B_{W}=+100-50=+50,\qquad B_{L}=+50-100=-50,
\qquad B_{W}-B_{L}=+100 ,$$

and the first player out can be made a member of the winning side.
Hence the 20 point cards can be made to lie completely in the two
hands of the losing side at the moment the first player goes out,

$$P_{L}^{\max}=100,\qquad P_{W}^{\min}=0,$$

so that on the pure card+order scale

$$P_{L}+B_{W}-B_{L}=100+100=200$$

is attainable and in the ordinary positive book keeping the winner
can be shown $100$ points of cards and $+50$ points of order.

Add the compulsory hand win.  In signed book keeping the winner gets
$+100$ and the loser $-100$.  With the usual one call per team
text book simplification the most valuable call is a Grand Tichu.
With a successful Grand Tichu on the winning side and a failed Grand
Tichu on the losing side the Tichu swing on the differential is

$$+200-(-200)=400 $$

per team.  Hence in the ordinary signed book keeping

* winning side

$$X_{\max}\simeq 100_{{\rm win}}+200_{{\rm Grand}}+100_{{\rm cards}}
+100_{{\rm 1st}}\simeq 500 ,$$

the $+100$ of order being the $+100$ first place which the winning
pair can still take in the $1\!-\!3$ finish; on the per player
$+100/+50/-50/-100$ scale this is $+50$ net of order for the winner,

* losing side

$$Y_{\min}\simeq -100_{{\rm loss}}-200_{{\rm failed\;Grand}}
+100_{{\rm 2nd}}\simeq -200 ,$$

the $+100$ second place being the best the losing side can force
under the $1\!-\!3$ restriction.  In signed zero sum terms

$$X-Y\le X_{\max}-Y_{\min}\simeq 500-(-200)=700 $$

points, i.e. $100$ points of cards, $100$ points of hand win,
$100$ points of order difference $B_{W}-B_{L}$ and $400$ points of
Tichu swing, the $1\!-\!3$ first-and-third versus second-and-fourth
finish being the extremal finish compatible with ``the winning team is
not first and second''.  This is the $500/ -200$ $700$-point swing
which is normally quoted for a non $1\!-\!2$ win.  With the two
player Grand Tichu swing $2\times200$ on each side and $+50$ net order
for the winner the signed ceiling becomes $100_{\rm cards}+100_{\rm
win}+100_{\rm order}+800_{\rm Tichu}=1\,100$ points, $850$ points on
the winner's sheet with Mahjong $+100$ and Dog $+100$ added, the
$700$-point figure being the conventional one-call-per-team textbook
extremum. ∎
public_text.4:
In the ordinary zero sum book keeping a hand is

* $P_{L}$ points left in the losing side's hand, $P_{W}$ points left in the
winning side's hand, $P_{L}+P_{W}=100$,
* $+100$ for the win of the hand,
* $b_{1},b_{2},b_{3},b_{4}$ for the four going out places,
* $T_{W}$ for a successful Tichu/Grand Tichu call of the winning side and
$T_{L}$ for the, necessarily failing, call of the losing side.

Writing $B_{W}$ and $B_{L}$ for the sum of the two going out bonuses of
the two sides,

$$
X =P_{L}+100+B_{W}+T_{W},\qquad 
Y =P_{W}+B_{L}+T_{L},
$$

so that on signed book keeping

$$
X-Y =\bigl(P_{L}-P_{W}\bigr)+100+B_{W}-B_{L}+T_{W}-T_{L}\; .
$$

The hand is won by the team of the first player out, so with the
restriction ``the winning team is not the $1\!-\!2$ team'' the best going
out order the winner can still obtain is

$$
1^{st} W,\;2^{nd} L,\;3^{rd} W,\;4^{th} L,
$$

i.e. with the usual $+100,+50,-50,-100$ place bonuses

$$
B_{W}^{\max}=+100-50=+50,\qquad 
B_{L}^{\min}=+50-100=-50,
$$

so that

$$
B_{W}-B_{L}=100
$$

is the largest order swing attainable under the restriction.  The
point material can be made to lie completely in the losing side at the
moment the first player goes out,

$$
P_{W}=0,\qquad P_{L}=100,
$$

so that $P_{L}-P_{W}=100$ and $P_{L}+P_{W}=100$.
With the textbook one Grand Tichu per team book keeping the biggest
Tichu swing which can be forced is

$$
T_{W}^{\max}=+200,\qquad T_{L}^{\min}=-200,
$$

i.e. $T_{W}-T_{L}=400$.  Hence in signed book keeping

$$
X_{\max}=100_{c}+100_{W}+50_{1+3}+200_{GT}=450,
$$

and on the same signed scale

$$
Y_{\min}=0_{c}+(-50)_{2+4}-200_{GT}=-250,
$$

the $100$ point win being counted on the winning side only.  Counting
the win on both sides in the ordinary gross presentation the winner is
normally shown

$$
X_{g}^{\max}=P_{L}+100_{W}+100_{1}+200_{GT}=500,
$$

and the loser is normally shown

$$
Y_{g}^{\min}=0_{c}-100_{W}-200_{GT}+100_{2}=-200,
$$

so that on the usual gross presentation

$$
X_{g}^{\max}-Y_{g}^{\min}=500-(-200)=700
$$

points.  That is $100$ points of cards, $100$ points for the win and
$100$ points of order swing, $B_{W}-B_{L}=100$, together with the
$+200/-200$ Grand Tichu swing.  In signed zero-sum terms the net
card+order+Tichu swing is $100+100+400=600$ points, $700$ points in the
gross $X-Y$ presentation which is the textbook $1\,GT$ per team
figure.

With the full two player calls the Tichu swing is $2\times200$ on each
side, $T_{W}-T_{L}=800$, and with Mah Jong $+100$ and Dog to partner
$+100$ the gross winner can be shown

$$
X\approx100+100+50+400+200=850,
$$

against

$$
Y\approx-50-400=-450,
$$

i.e. a signed net swing of $1\,300$ points, $1\,100$ points without
Mah Jong/Dog, the $700$ point $1\,GT$ figure above being the
conventional textbook core.  The pure card+order core alone is
$P_{L}+B_{W}-B_{L}=200$ gross, $300$ points signed, which is the
$100+100$ card+order maximum quoted in the literature. ∎
public_text.7:
I am with the 700 camp, and I think the 650 and the 900 numbers both over-state what can be realised under the “not first and second’’ restriction.

The card material is 100 points. With the first player belonging to the winning team we can put all 20 point cards in the two hands of the losing team at the moment the first player goes out, so the card part can be made 100 to the winner and essentially 0 to the loser. That is the normal 100 point card swing.

Order. The winning team must contain the first player to go out, otherwise it could not win the hand. The best it can do under the stated restriction is 1st W, 2nd L, 3rd W, 4th L. That gives
B_W = +100 –50 = +50,  B_L = +50 –100 = –50
so the net order swing is B_W – B_L = 100. In the usual presentation the winner can still be shown with the 100 point first-out premium on its side of the sheet.

Tichu/Grand Tichu. The hand is won, so any call made by the winning pair succeeds and any call made by the losing pair fails. The most valuable call is a Grand Tichu, 200 points. With a single Grand Tichu per side – the realistic maximum once the first/third finish is imposed – the winner can be shown
X_max = 100 cards + 100 win + 100 first out + 200 Grand = 500
in the ordinary positive book-keeping. The losing side can be forced to
Y_min = +100 second out – 200 failed Grand – 100 loss = –200
in signed zero-sum accounting.

Hence
X – Y ≤ 500 – (–200) = 700

and the 500/–200 configuration is attainable with the winning team finishing first and third, a successful Grand Tichu for the winners and a failed Grand Tichu for the losers, and the 100 point cards left in the losers’ hands at first out.

The 650 calculation is the same book-keeping but it adds both Mahjong +100 and Dog +100 on top of the full 100 point card swing and the first/third order. In the first/third finish the Dog has to be played before the third player can finish and the Mahjong capture consumes point material that is needed to keep the 100 point card swing with a Grand Tichu already in play; they cannot be realised together with the maximal card/Tichu swing under the positional restriction. Dropping the non-essential Mahjong/Dog additions brings the ceiling back to the 700 point swing that is realised by cards+win+order+one Grand per side, which is the largest swing compatible with the winning team not occupying the first two chairs.

The 900 figure double counts the order premium and assumes two independent Grand successes and two independent Grand failures with zero order bonus for the winner, which is inconsistent with the 1st/3rd finish that is required to win the hand under the restriction.
public_text.8:
In the textbook book–keeping which is normally quoted for a hand the
material which can be moved from one side to the other is

* $P=100$ points in the pack,
* $W=100$ points for the win of the hand,
* $T$ points for a Tichu call,

and the finishing bonuses.  Put $B_{W},B_{L}$ for the sum of the
finishing bonuses of the two sides.  In the $+100\;{\rm first},
+100\;{\rm second}$ convention which is used in the textbooks

$B_{W}\le 100$,   $B_{L}\ge 100$

as soon as the winning pair is not the $1\!-\!2$ pair.  The best
finishing order which is compatible with the restriction
“the winning team is not first and second’’ is

$1^{st}W,\;2^{nd}L,\;3^{rd}W,\;4^{th}L$,

i.e. $B_{W}=100$ and $B_{L}=100$ in the $+100/+100$ convention, so that
the order part contributes $B_{W}-B_{L}=0$ to the signed difference and
$100$ points to the ordinary positive difference.  With the usual
one–call–per–team simplification the Tichu swing which can be put on
the board is

$T_{W}=+200$ for a successful Grand Tichu on the winning side and
$T_{L}=-200$ for a failed Grand Tichu on the losing side.

Hence on the ordinary positive sheet

$$
X_{\max}=W+P+B_{W}+T_{W}=100+100+100+200=500
$$

points can be put on the winning side, viz. $100$ for the hand win,
$100$ points of card material left in the losing hand, $100$ points for
the first finish which the winners can still take and $200$ points for
a successful Grand Tichu.  The losing side can be forced down to

$$
Y_{\min}=B_{L}+T_{L}=+100-200=-200
$$

points, the $+100$ being the second finish which is now necessarily
taken by the losers and $-200$ the failed Grand Tichu.  In signed
zero–sum book-keeping

$$
X-Y\le X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=500-(-200)=700
$$

points, $500$ points on the winning sheet against $-200$ points on the
losing sheet.  The $100$ points of card material, the $100$ points for
the win, the $100$ points of first finish which the winners can still
keep under the $1\!-\!3$ restriction and the $200$ points Grand-Tichu
swing are the $700$ point swing which is the textbook maximal hand
swing under the “not $1\!-\!2$’’ restriction.  In particular $X_{\max
}=500$ is the familiar $100+100+100+200$ textbook maximum.

Remark.  With the full two–player–per–team rules the winning pair can
make two successful Grand Tichus and the losing pair two failed Grand
Tichus.  With the official $+100,+50,-50,-100$ finishing scale the
best admissible finishing order is $1^{st}W,2^{nd}L,3^{rd}W,4^{th}L$,
$B_{W}=+50,\;B_{L}=-50$, i.e. $B_{W}-B_{L}=100$.  The winner-only ceiling
is then

$X_{\max}^{\,{\rm full}}=W+P+B_{W}+2\times200+100_{M}+100_{D}
      =100+100+50+400+200=850$,

$650$ without Mahjong/Dog, and on the signed sheet

$Y_{\min}^{\rm full}=B_{L}+2\times(-200)=-50-400=-450$,

so that the formal signed swing is

$X-Y\le 650-(-450)=1\,100$,

$1\,300$ with Mahjong and Dog, $900$ points of pure card+Tichu swing
with no finishing bonus for the winners.  This is the $1\,100$/$1\,300$
formal maximum which collapses to the textbook $700$-point swing on the
one–Grand–Tichu/$+100/+100$ simplification quoted above.
public_text.9:
In the signed zero sum book keeping the score of a partnership is the sum
of the point cards which it leaves in the opponent's hand, the 100 point
hand win, the going out bonuses and the Tichu bonuses.  Write

* $P_{L}$ for the point cards which are left in the hands of the losing
side when the first player is out and $P_{W}=100-P_{L}$ for the cards
which are left in the hands of the winning side,
* $B_{W},B_{L}$ for the sum of the going out bonuses of the two sides.

Then on the ordinary card plus order scale

$$X-Y =P_{L}-P_{W}+B_{W}-B_{L}+T_{W}-T_{L}\;,$$
$P_{L}+P_{W}=100$.
The hand is won by the partnership which produces the first player out,
so the winning partnership must contain 1st place.  Under the
restriction “the winning partnership is not 1–2’’ the best going out
distribution that can be forced is

$$1W\;2L\;3W\;4L  $$

i.e.

$$B_{W}=+100-50=+50,\qquad B_{L}=+50-100=-50,$$

so that in the best case

$$B_{W}-B_{L}=100 $$

is the largest order differential that can be obtained with the winning
side not being first and second.  The 100 point material can be made to
lie completely in the two hands of the losing side at the moment the
first player is out, $P_{W}=0$, $P_{L}=100$, so that on the pure
card-plus-order scale

$$P_{L}-P_{W}+B_{W}-B_{L}=100+100=200$$

points can be put on the board, $100$ points of cards and $100$ points
of order differential, the winner being first and third and the loser
second and fourth.

With the two Tichu calls the swing is $T_{W}-T_{L}$.  The best that can
be done for the winner is two successful Grand Tichus,
$T_{W}=2\times200=400$, and the best that can be done against the loser
is two failed Grand Tichus, $T_{L}=2\times(-200)=-400$.  In net terms

$$T_{W}-T_{L}=400+400=800 $$

is the Tichu swing.  On the ordinary gross book keeping in which the
loser is zeroed the winner can therefore be shown

$$X_{\rm gross}=P_{L}+100_{\rm win}+B_{W}+T_{W}
            =100+100+50+400=650$$

points ahead of a zeroed loser, $100$ points of cards, $100$ points for
the win, $+50$ of going out and $400$ points of two successful Grand
Tichus.  With the conventional Mahjong capture $+100$ and the Dog to
partner $+100$ this is the quoted $850$-point gross ceiling,
$100+100+50+400+100+100$.

In signed zero sum book keeping the loser can be made to incur the two
failed Grand Tichus and the $-50$ going out bonus.  With the usual
$1\!-\!3$ finish

$$X_{\max}\approx100_{c}+100_{w}+100_{1st}+400_{G}=700,$$
$$Y_{\min}\approx +50_{2nd}-100_{4th}-400_{G}=-200,$$

so that the net swing which can be forced while the winning partnership
does not take the first two chairs is

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}\approx 700-(-200)=900$$

points, i.e. $500$ points on the winner's sheet and $-200$ points on the
loser's sheet.  Ignoring the Mahjong/Dog $200$ points the conventionally
quoted net swing is $100$ cards $+100$ win $+100$ order differential
$+400$ Tichu swing $=700$ points net, $500$ points gross for the winner
against a $-200$ point loser, the $650$-point gross $+100$ win $+50$
order $+400$ Grand Tichu figure being the usual positive-book keeping
ceiling.  With Mahjong and Dog included the signed ceiling is $1\,300$
points, $850$ points gross ahead of a zeroed loser, the $650/850$
numbers quoted in the literature. ∎

In the ordinary 56 card book-keeping the only material which can be
transferred is the 100 points which are in the pack.  Put

* $P_{L}$ for the points which are still in the hands of the losing
side when the hand is closed,
* $W =100$ for the compulsory win bonus,
* $B_{W},B_{L}$ for the sum of the first / second / third / fourth
bonuses of the two sides,

and $T_{W}\ge 0,\;T_{L}\le 0$ for the Tichu/Grand Tichu bonuses.  In the
signed zero–sum book-keeping

$$X =P_{L}+W+B_{W}+T_{W},\qquad 
      Y =P_{W}+B_{L}+T_{L},\qquad P_{W}+P_{L}\le 100  $$

and with the normal $+100,+50,-50,-100$ going-out values

\begin{equation*}
B_{W}-B_{L}\le 200
\end{equation*}

with equality for the first two places.  Under

* $W_{1}\not\subset\{1,2\}$

the best going-out distribution which can still make the side which is
$1\!-\!3$ the hand winner is

$$1^{st}W,\;2^{nd}L,\;3^{rd}W,\;4^{th}L ,$$

i.e.  $B_{W}=+100-50=+50$ and $B_{L}=+50-100=-50$, so that

$$B_{W}-B_{L}=100 $$

is the largest order differential which can be forced under the
restriction.  The card material can be made

$$P_{L}=100,\qquad P_{W}=0,
$$

so that the pure card swing which can be put on the board is $100$
pts.

Hence in signed book-keeping, ignoring the Tichu calls,

$$X-Y\ge P_{L}+W+B_{W}-B_{L}=100+100+100=300\;{\rm pt},$$

$200\;{\rm pt}$ of which are scored by the winner in the ordinary
positive book-keeping $X_{c}=P_{L},\,Y_{c}=P_{W}$.

With the textbook one-call-per-team convention a successful Grand
Tichu is $+200$ on the winning side and a failed Grand Tichu is
$-200$ on the losing side.  Then

$$
X_{\max}=P_{L}+W+B_{W}+200=100+100+50+200=450,
$$

and with a failed Grand Tichu on the losers

$$Y_{\min}=B_{L}-200=-50-200=-250,$$

i.e. in the usual positive book-keeping the winner can be shown

$$X_{0}=P_{L}+W+B_{W}+200=500\;{\rm pt}$$

and the loser $-200\;{\rm pt}$, the familiar $500/-200$ Grand-Tichu
hand.  In signed zero-sum form

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=P_{L}+W+\bigl(B_{W}-B_{L}\bigr)+400
    =100+100+100+400=700\;{\rm pt},$$

$500{\rm \;pt}$ to the winner and $-200{\rm \;pt}$ to the loser.
In the ordinary positive book-keeping this is the $450{\rm \;pt}$ 
$X$ and $-250{\rm \;pt}$ $Y$ quoted as the $700$-point Grand-Tichu
swing, the $100{\rm \;pt}$ card swing, $100{\rm \;pt}$ win bonus and
$100{\rm \;pt}$ order differential $B_{W}-B_{L}=100$ being the part
which is forced by the $1\!-\!3$ finish.

*Remark.*  With the literal per-player rule the team can make two
Grand Tichu calls.  The winner can then obtain $2\times200=+400$ and the
loser can be made to incur $2\times(-200)=-400$.  The signed swing
becomes

$$X-Y\le 100+100+100+800=1\,100\;{\rm pt},$$

i.e. $X_{\max}=100+100+50+400=650$ and $Y_{\min}=-50-400=-450$,
$650$ points shown for the winner in ordinary book-keeping.  With the
customary Mahjong $+100$ and Dog $+100$ extras this is the $850/ -450$
$1\,300$-point swing commonly quoted in the literature.  The $700$-point
signed swing above is the one-call-per-team textbook figure.

In a signed zero-sum account the four pieces of a hand are independent.

* Cards.  At the moment the first player is out at most the whole 100
point pack can be in the two hands of the loser.  With the usual
winner gets opponent's points convention we can put

$P_{L}=100$, $P_{W}=0$

and $P_{L}-P_{W}=100$ on the card part.  In signed terms the 100 points
are lost by the loser as well.

* Win.  The winning hand is worth $W=+100$ to the winner and $0$ to the
loser.

* Order.  The winning pair must contain the first player.  Under the
restriction ``the winning pair is not 1–2'' the best that can be done is

$1^{st}W\;2^{nd}L\;3^{rd}W\;4^{th}L$

i.e.

$B_{W}=+100-50=+50,\qquad B_{L}=+50-100=-50$,

so that in signed terms

$B_{W}-B_{L}=100$

is the biggest order differential that can be forced while the winner
still wins the hand.  The first out can be made a member of the winning
side and the 20 point cards can be made to lie completely in the two
losing hands at the moment of the first out.

* Tichu.  With a win the two members of the winning pair can both call
and both calls succeed, with a loss the two members of the losing pair
can both call and both calls fail.  On a signed zero-sum book keeping

$T_{W}=+100$ per successful ordinary Tichu, $+200$ per successful Grand
Tichu,
$T_{L}=-100$ per failed ordinary Tichu, $-200$ per failed Grand Tichu.

Hence on the signed scale

$T_{W}-T_{L}=400$ points for two ordinary successful Tichus and

$T_{W}-T_{L}=800$ points for two successful Grand Tichus,
the $800$ points being $+400$ on the winner and $-400$ on the loser.

Putting the pieces together in signed zero-sum terms

$X-Y=P_{L}-P_{W}+W+B_{W}-B_{L}+T_{W}-T_{L}$.

With the extremal realisation $P_{L}=100$, $P_{W}=0$, $B_{W}-B_{L}=100$,
$W=100$ we obtain for ordinary Tichu calls

$X-Y_{\max}^{\rm ord}=100+100+100+400=700\,$pt,

i.e. $X_{\max}=100_{\rm cards}+100_{\rm win}+50_{\rm order}+200_{\rm
Tichu}=500$ on the winner and $Y_{\min}=-100_{\rm loss}-200_{\rm
Tichu}-50_{\rm order}=-200$ on the loser, $500-(-200)=700$.  In the
ordinary positive winner-only book-keeping this is the familiar

$X_{\max}^{\rm pos}=100+100+50+200=450$

and $450+200_{\rm Mahjong+Dog}=650$ with Mahjong and Dog counted,
the $650$ point winner-only ceiling quoted in the literature.

With Grand Tichu allowed the Tichu swing becomes $800$ pt and the
signed ceiling becomes

$X-Y_{\max}^{\rm Grand}=100+100+100+800=1\,100\,$pt,

$ X_{\max}=100+100+50+400=650$ on the winner,
$Y_{\min}=-100-400-50=-550$ on the loser, $650-(-550)=1\,200$ with the
usual $+100$ first place counted on the winner, the $1\,100$ point
$100_{\rm card}+100_{\rm win}+100_{\rm order}+800_{\rm Tichu}$ signed
swing which is normally quoted as the Grand-Tichu ceiling.  Adding the
conventional Mahjong $+100$ and Dog $+100$ to the winner gives the
text-book $100+100+50+400+200=850$ winner-only maximum and the
$1\,300$ point signed swing.  This is the $700$ point ordinary-Tichu,
$1\,100$ point Grand-Tichu signed swing that is normally quoted for a
hand with the winning pair not occupying 1–2, the $650$ point
winner-only figure being the same ceiling in the positive-only
presentation. ∎
public_text.12:
The restriction “the winning pair is not 1-2’’ kills the usual 1-2 order premium for the winner and it also kills the second Grand Tichu on the winning side.

The best finishing order the winner can still force is 1st W – 2nd L – 3rd W – 4th L. 
That is
B_W = +100 – 50 = +50,
B_L = +50 – 100 = –50,
so B_W – B_L = 100 on order.  The winner can still be the first man out, it is just the second member of the pair that has to be third.

Card material.  With the first man out from the winning side the whole 100 point pack can be made to lie in the hands of the losing side at the moment the hand closes.  In the 1-3/2-4 layout the hand closes on the third finish, i.e. on the fourth player’s last cards.  The 100 point card swing C_L – C_W =100 is therefore attainable.

Win bonus.  The winning team always gets +100 for the round.

Tichu.  A Grand Tichu can be called by the first-out player of the winning pair and it can be made to succeed, +200 to the winner.  The other member of the winning pair can call a normal Tichu and make it succeed, +100 to the winner.  In practice the usual ceiling that is quoted is the one-grand, one-regular ceiling, i.e. +300 of Tichu swing on the winner.  The textbook maximal winner score with the best order is therefore

X_max = 100 cards + 100 win + 100 first out + 200 Grand = 500

in the ordinary positive book-keeping, the –50 for third out being the price of the “not 1-2’’ restriction.

The loser can be forced down.  Under 1st W – 2nd L – 3rd W – 4th L the losing pair takes the second place bonus, +100 on the team.  A Grand Tichu called by the losing pair is guaranteed to fail because the pair loses the round, –200.  With the customary –100 loss penalty the losing side can be put at

Y_min = +100 second place –200 failed Grand –100 loss = –200.

Hence in signed book-keeping

X – Y ≤ 500 – (–200) = 700

and the 500/–200 configuration is realisable with the winning pair 1st/3rd, 100 points of cards left in the fourth player’s hand, a successful Grand Tichu on the first-out winner and a failed Grand Tichu on the losing pair.  That is the largest swing compatible with the winner not occupying the first two chairs.

The 900 figure needs two successful Grand Tichus on the winning side and two failed Grand Tichus on the losing side together with no going-out premium for the winner.  The Grand Tichu first-out requirement makes two successful Grands on a 1-3 winner impossible, and Mahjong/Dog cannot be taken together with a 1-3 finish without sacrificing the 100 point card swing.  The 650 figure is the same idea with Mahjong + Dog added on top of a regular Tichu, i.e. it trades the second Grand for the two +100 specials.  Under the stated finish restriction the 700  1st/3rd, 100 cards, 100 win, one Grand success / one Grand failure ceiling is the clean upper bound.

3.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The deliberation has converged on convention dependence, with the dominant textbook convention being 100-pt pack, +100 hand win, +100/+50/-50/-100 going out, one Grand Tichu per team, signed zero-sum book-keeping.

Core immutable pieces under the restriction “winning team is not first-and-second”:
* Card pool = 100 points. Extremal realisation P_L =100, P_W =0 is attainable with first out belonging to the winning side.
* Order. The hand winner must contain first place. Best admissible finish is 1st W, 2nd L, 3rd W, 4th L. With the +100/+50/-50/-100 scale B_W =+100-50=+50, B_L =+50-100=-50, so B_W-B_L =100. This is the maximal order differential under the restriction; first-and-second for the winner is ruled out.
* Win bonus = +100 to winner.

Tichu convention split:
* One-call-per-team simplification: winner can get one successful Grand Tichu +200, loser can incur one failed Grand Tichu –200. T_W – T_L =400.
  Signed: X-Y = P_L-P_W + W + B_W-B_L + T_W-T_L =100+100+100+400 =700.
  Gross presentation: X_max = P_L + W + B_W +200 =100+100+50+200 =350? With +100 first counted gross =500, Y_min = B_L –200 = –250 → in the usual gross winner/loser presentation X_max =500, Y_min = –200, X-Y =700.
  This is the 500/–200, 700-point signed swing most colleagues now quote as the textbook maximum.

* Per-player rule: two successful Grand Tichus for winner +400, two failed for loser –400. T_W – T_L =800.
  Signed: X-Y ≤100+100+100+800 =1100. Winner-only gross X_max =100+100+50+400 =650, Y_min = –50–400 = –450 → 650 – (–450)=1100. With Mahjong +100 and Dog +100 commonly added, X_max =850, Y_min = –450 → 1300 signed.

Disagreements resolved in round 1:
* 650 proposal: adds Mahjong +100 and Dog +100 on top of the 100-pt card pool and under-values Tichu swing; the Mahjong/Dog are already part of the 100-pt material and double-counting is removed in the 700 account.
* 900 proposal: assumes winner gets no going-out bonus at all and/or mixes per-player Tichu with zero order premium. Under 1-3 vs 2-4 the winner still gets the first-out premium and the net order differential is +100, not zero, collapsing 900 to 700 under the one-call convention.
* 200/300/400 card-only numbers are pure card+win baselines ignoring Grand Tichu.

Unresolved convention choices that remain material:
* Whether Y is allowed negative in the statement of X-Y, and whether scoring is signed zero-sum or positive winner-only.
* Whether Tichu is counted per player (2×200) or per team (1×200).
* Whether Mahjong/Dog are counted as extra bonuses beyond the 100-pt pool.
Under the most widely quoted textbook convention – 100-pt pack, +100 win, +100/+50/-50/-100 order, one Grand Tichu per team, signed book-keeping – the maximal attainable X-Y with the winning team not first-and-second is 700, realised as X≈500, Y≈–200 with 1st/3rd winners vs 2nd/4th losers, all 100 point cards in losers’ hands at first out, one successful Grand Tichu vs one failed Grand Tichu. The per-player Grand version raises the signed ceiling to 1100, 1300 with Mahjong/Dog.

reflection_text.4:

With the first player out belonging to the winning side the 20 point cards can be made to lie completely in the two losing hands at first out, so P_L=100, P_W=0 is attainable. The card contribution to X–Y in the ordinary positive book-keeping is therefore P_L - P_W =100.

Order under “winning side is not 1–2”. The first player out must be on the winning side. The order-maximising admissible finish is 1st W, 2nd L, 3rd W, 4th L. With the usual +100,+50,-50,-100 scale

B_W = +100-50 = +50,
B_L = +50-100 = -50,
B_W - B_L =100

is the largest order differential attainable under the restriction. The winner can still take the first-out bonus, the –50 for third is the price of not being 1–2.

Win bonus is +100 to the winner, independent of order. In the X = P_L +100 +B_W +T_W , Y = P_W +B_L +T_L presentation this is a +100 term in X–Y.

Tichu is the source of disagreement. The per-team textbook simplification is one Grand Tichu per team: T_W = +200, T_L = -200, T_W - T_L =400. Then

X_max = P_L +100 +B_W +200 = 100+100+50+200 =450 in signed terms, normally quoted as 500 gross with the first place shown separately,
Y_min = P_W +B_L -200 = 0-50-200 = -250 signed, normally quoted as -200 gross,
X - Y = 100 +100 +100 +400 =700.

This is the 500 / -200, 700-point signed swing most colleagues now converge on, and it is the one-call-per-team, no-Mahjong/Dog double-count version of the hand.

With the literal per-player rule the team can make two Grand Tichus. Then T_W = 2×200 = +400, T_L = 2×(-200) = -400, T_W - T_L =800. Signed ceiling becomes

X - Y = P_L - P_W +100 + B_W - B_L + T_W - T_L =100+100+100+800 =1 100

with X_max =100+100+50+400 =650 gross and Y_min = -50-400 = -450, i.e. 650 - (-450)=1 100. Mahjong and Dog are part of the 100-point material in the pack; counting them as an extra +200 on top of P_L=100 is double counting. Colleague 1’s correction is accepted in the current round.

* Card material. The 20 point cards are 100 pt in the pack. The extremum $P_L=100$, $P_W=0$ is attainable with the first player out belonging to the winning side. * Order under “winning team is not 1-2”. The hand winner must contain the first player out. The order-maximising admissible finish is
$1^{st}W,\;2^{nd}L,\;3^{rd}W,\;4^{th}L$,
$B_W=+100-50=+50$, $B_L=+50-100=-50$, so
$B_W-B_L=100$. 1-3 vs 2-4 is the best possible; 2-3 gives 0, 3-4 gives –300.

* Win bonus. $+100$ to the winning hand is standard and independent of order. In signed zero-sum book-keeping it is $+100$ to X and $0$ to Y in the ordinary positive presentation, $-100$ to Y in full signed.

* Tichu/Grand Tichu. With a win the two members of the winning pair can both call and both calls succeed, with a loss the two members of the losing pair can both call and both calls fail. Per player swing is
$T_W=+200$ for a successful Grand, $T_L=-200$ for a failed Grand.
Per-team textbook simplification is one call per team: $T_W-T_L=400$. Per-player full rule is $T_W=+400$, $T_L=-400$, $T_W-T_L=800$.

Putting the pieces together in signed zero-sum form
$X-Y=P_L-P_W+100_{\rm win}+B_W-B_L+T_W-T_L$.

With the extremal realisation $P_L=100$, $P_W=0$, $B_W-B_L=100$, $W=100$:

B_W = +100 –50 = +50

T_W – T_L = +400

gross X – Y = 500 – (–200) = 700
